types.name: BloomScheduler
types.doc: Plugin-owned task scheduling with automatic cleanup. Every task is owned by the Bloom instance that created it and is cancelled when Bloom shuts down. Exceptions thrown by tasks are caught and logged with the task's origin; they never kill the scheduler. Threading rules • sync* tasks run on the main server thread. Use them for anything that touches worlds, entities, players, inventories or most other Bukkit API. • async* tasks run on a background thread. Use them for I/O, computation and network calls. Never modify worlds, entities or inventories from an async task: hop back with sync or mainThreadExecutor. Delays and periods are in server ticks (20 per second at full speed) unless a Duration overload is used. A delay of 0 means "the next tick".

types.name: TextFormat
types.doc: The markup language used to write a message. Both formats work on every supported platform: • On modern Paper, MINIMESSAGE is parsed by the real MiniMessage library and LEGACY by Adventure's legacy serializer. • On legacy servers, LEGACY is native, and MINIMESSAGE is converted by Bloom's MiniMessage subset converter: named colours, hex colours (downsampled to the nearest legacy colour), decorations, <reset> and <newline>. Interactive tags (click, hover, insertion) and gradients are rendered as plain text content without their effect.

modules.name: bloom-bukkit
modules.description: Bloom for Bukkit-family servers: Bloom entry point, platform detection, adapter SPI, scheduler, messaging and events.

types.name: Bloom
types.doc: The Bloom entry point for Bukkit-family plugins. public final class MyPlugin extends JavaPlugin { private Bloom bloom; @Override public void onEnable() { bloom = Bloom.enable(this); bloom.messages().send(getServer().getConsoleSender(), "&dBloom is ready on {platform}", Placeholder.of("platform", bloom.platform().describe())); } @Override public void onDisable() { if (bloom != null) { bloom.shutdown(); } } } enable detects the server, selects the matching version adapter, starts core services and logs a startup banner. If the server is not supported it throws BloomStartupException with an explanation; let it propagate from onEnable (the server then disables the plugin) or catch it to disable gracefully. In embedded mode each plugin has its own relocated copy of Bloom, so get returns the instance of the calling plugin.

Events events = bloom.events(); events.subscribe(PlayerJoinEvent.class, event -> messages.send(event.getPlayer(), "&dWelcome!")); events.listen(PlayerInteractEvent.class) .priority(EventPriority.HIGH) .ignoreCancelled() .filter(event -> event.getItem() != null) .limit(1) .handler(event -> event.getPlayer().sendMessage("First interaction!")); Handlers run on the thread that fires the event: the main thread for most events, a background thread for asynchronous events such as AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent. types.name: Messenger
types.doc: Sends formatted text to players and the console on every supported platform. Obtain the default instance with bloom.messages(); derive variants with withPrefix, withFormat and withUnsupportedPolicy. Messengers are immutable and thread-safe. Messenger messages = bloom.messages().withPrefix("&d&lBloom &8» "); messages.send(player, "&7Welcome back, &f{player}&7!", Placeholder.of("player", player.getName())); messages.actionBar(player, "&aSaved!"); messages.title(player, Title.of("&dLevel up", "&7You reached level {level}"), Placeholder.of("level", 5)); Threads Chat, action bars and titles may be sent from any thread. Boss bars must be created and changed on the main thread. Unsupported features Action bars, titles and boss bars depend on capabilities. When one is missing, behaviour follows the UnsupportedFeaturePolicy: skip with a one-time warning (default), fall back to chat, or throw.

types.signature: public final class Menus implements AutoCloseable
types.doc: Opens and manages menus. Obtain with of; the service registers its own listeners, so no per-menu listener registration is needed. types.name: YamlConfig
types.signature: public final class YamlConfig extends ConfigSection
types.doc: A YAML configuration file with bundled defaults, typed access, validation, migrations and safe writes. YamlConfig config = YamlConfig.builder(getDataFolder().toPath().resolve("config.yml")) .defaults(() -> getResource("config.yml")) .logger(getLogger()) .build(); // creates the file from defaults if missing, then loads it String prefix = config.getString("messages.prefix"); int maxHomes = config.getInt("homes.max", 3); Settings s = config.get("settings", Settings.class); // POJO mapping Safety • A missing file is created by copying the defaults resource byte-for-byte (comments included). • Existing files are never rewritten implicitly, except by migrations (which first copy the file to a timestamped .bak) and by Builder.addMissingDefaults (opt-in, also backed up). • save and migrations edit the file's YAML node tree, so comments and formatting of untouched keys are preserved. Writes are atomic (temporary file + move). • reload keeps the previous values if the new file is invalid. • A file whose version is newer than the plugin supports is rejected rather than downgraded. Values are loaded with SnakeYAML's SafeConstructor (no arbitrary object construction), duplicate keys are rejected and alias expansion is limited. Thread-safe.

types.name: Database
types.signature: public final class Database implements Terminable
types.doc: A pooled SQL database with an asynchronous API. Database db = Database.builder() .sqlite(getDataFolder().toPath().resolve("data.db")) .mainThreadCheck(bloom.scheduler()::isPrimaryThread) .logger(getLogger()) .build(); db.migrate(migrations).join(); // acceptable in onEnable: the server is not ticking yet db.queryOne("SELECT kills FROM stats WHERE uuid = ?", rs -> rs.getInt(1), player.getUniqueId()) .thenAcceptAsync(kills -> player.sendMessage("Kills: " + kills.orElse(0)), bloom.scheduler().mainThreadExecutor()); // back on the main thread Threading Operations run on a bounded pool of database threads (one per connection). Returned futures complete on those threads: switch to the main thread with thenAcceptAsync(..., mainThreadExecutor()) before touching game state. When the queue is full (default 1000 pending operations) new operations fail immediately with StorageException instead of piling up unbounded work. Shutdown close stops accepting work, waits for queued operations (default up to 10 s), fails any operation that could not run, and closes the pool. Call it in onDisable; when a Bloom instance owns it (registered in the service registry) Bloom closes it automatically.
